# Intake Brief: Ship skill invalidates audits

## Problem statement

Running `/skill:ship` leaves many work items reading as having an **out-of-date
("invalidated") audit**. The release close path writes to every item it
releases — `wl close --force --reason "Shipped in vX"` and
`wl update --status completed --stage done` (plus comments) — which bumps each
item's `updatedAt` well after its `auditedAt`. The freshness **time gate**
(`isAuditStale` in `skill/ship/scripts/audit-freshness.js`, mirrored by
`_check_audit_freshness` in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`) treats
`auditedAt < updatedAt − 60 s` (outside the 30 s persistence-write tolerance)
as stale. Only audits that carry a **v2 content fingerprint**
(`Audit content fingerprint (v2): …`) are immune, because the content-freshness
probe can confirm the item's title/description did not change; legacy/manual
audits (no v2 line) fall all the way back to the time gate and therefore
genuinely read as invalidated. Time-based consumers (e.g. the herdr
dispatcher's `isAuditFresh`) flag all of them.

## Users

- **Producers running a release** — user story: "When I run `/skill:ship` I
  don't want the audit panel to light up with 'out of date' on dozens of just-
  released items, forcing me to re-audit finished work just to clear the
  flags."
- **Audit operators / automated dispatchers** — user story: "I want audit
  freshness to reflect whether the audited content actually changed, not
  whether an unrelated lifecycle write (close, stage/status transition, sync)
  touched `updatedAt`."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **RCA documented.** Identify the exact ship/release steps that move
   `updatedAt` on released items and the exact freshness rule that then reports
   them stale, with representative item ids and timestamps as evidence (e.g.
   audited `2026-11-15T12:20:27Z`, re-staged to completed `12:27:05Z`, closed
   by ship `14:17:53Z`). Classify the affected audits: v2 content-fresh
   (protected by the probe) versus legacy/manual (time-gate only).
2. **Decision recorded — intended or avoidable.** State, with justification
   tied to the existing content-freshness contract, whether the invalidation is
   an intended side effect of the release writes or an avoidable defect, and
   which layer is at fault (release write path, freshness rule, or a display/
   dispatcher consumer).
3. **Fix if avoidable.** Implement the minimal change so that a ship run does
   not leave content-unchanged audits reading as out of date — for example,
   preserving the audit freshness signal through the close/re-stage write (a
   content fingerprint of the final description, or not bumping the audited
   timestamp semantics) — **without** re-running the expensive audit pipeline
   for the backlog and without weakening verdict semantics.
4. **Explain if intended.** If (and only if) the RCA proves the behaviour is
   intended, add the missing explanation to the affected work item and docs so
   the side effect and its rationale are recorded — including any display-only
   consumer (herdr) that should be scoped out with a linked item.
5. **Targeted tests.** Add or extend tests that lock the chosen behaviour:
   a lifecycle-only `updatedAt` bump after a v2 audit still reports fresh; a
   content (title/description) change still invalidates; and the legacy/manual
   fallback behaves as documented. Tests must exercise production code, not
   re-implement it.
6. **Documentation updated.** Update `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`,
   `skill/audit/SKILL.md` and `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`
   (plus any relevant wiki/docs-site entry) to reflect the change or decision.
7. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Impact

After a release, producers stop seeing content-unchanged work items flagged as
"audit out of date", so they no longer have to re-audit finished work just to
clear spurious staleness.

## Constraints

- **Verdict semantics unchanged:** freshness only decides when an audit is
  reused or how staleness is displayed; it never changes what an audit
  concludes. `--force` still bypasses the gate.
- **No mass re-audit:** any fix must not fan out the full audit pipeline across
  the in-review/backlog set; the content-freshness fast path and bounded
  remediation must keep their cost profile.
- **Read-only probes stay read-only:** no test-suite execution or pi calls from
  the freshness probe.
- **Preserve the existing content-fresh fast path** (`hasContentFingerprint` /
  `queryContentFreshness` / `attemptAuditRemediation`) and child-reuse gate.
- **Repository boundary:** the herdr/ContextHub dispatcher (`isAuditFresh` in
  `packages/herdr/src/icons.ts`) is a different repository; if the RCA shows a
  change there is required, file a linked item rather than editing it here.

## Existing state

- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` — release close path. Around lines
  700–735 it invokes `wl close <id> --force --reason "Shipped in vX"`,
  `wl update <child> --status completed --stage done`, and `wl comment add`.
  Each write bumps `updatedAt`; none changes the item's title or description.
- `skill/ship/scripts/audit-freshness.js` — `isAuditStale()` is the shared
  time gate. An audit is fresh only when `auditedAt > updatedAt + 60 s`, or
  when `updatedAt` is 0–30 s after `auditedAt` (the audit's own persistence
  write). Everything else is stale.
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` — `getAuditStatus()` reports
  `stale` for a passing-but-time-stale audit; `hasContentFingerprint()` only
  matches the **v2** line; `queryContentFreshness()` calls
  `audit_runner.py check-freshness <id> --json`, which resolves a time-stale
  audit as fresh when the v2 fingerprint still matches. Legacy/unversioned
  fingerprints are deliberately not matched and fall back to the time gate.
- `skill/ship/scripts/refresh-audits.js` — `planAuditRefresh()` classifies a
  passing-but-time-stale audit as `toRefresh` (it consults the time gate, not
  the content probe), so ship pre-flight can plan re-audits of content-fresh
  items; the runner then short-circuits, but the stored `auditedAt` is not
  re-stamped, so a time-based consumer keeps seeing it as out of date.
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_check_audit_freshness()` (~line
  2380) is the authoritative freshness gate (v2 content gate, then 60 s time
  gate with the 30 s persistence tolerance). On a content-fresh short-circuit
  it returns the stored report **without** re-stamping `auditedAt`.
  `AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_PREFIX` (~line 1434) is
  `"Audit content fingerprint (v2): "`; `_compute_content_fingerprint()` (~line
  3111) hashes `{schema: 2, title_hash, description_hash}` with zero git calls.
- `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` — documents the
  content-freshness contract: "content-fresh audits are trusted regardless of
  `updatedAt` … a `wl sync`-moved `updatedAt` can never force a re-audit of
  unchanged content" (Step 2 audit gate section, ~lines 200–232).
- **Observed evidence (current store):** of 1 685 audited, non-deleted items,
  1 274 are time-stale and 1 272 of those are completed; **1 155** of the stale
  audits carry no v2 fingerprint line (legacy or manual "Approved by manual
  review" audits), and 119 stale audits do carry a v2 line (content changed
  after the audit). Example `SA-0MWE1EAR30045VHO`: audited
  `2026-11-15T12:20:27Z`, cascaded to completed `12:27:05Z`, closed by ship
  `14:17:53Z`; `check-freshness` still reports **fresh** (v2 content match)
  even though the time gate calls it stale. Example `SA-0MWE4BT63005N8OE`:
  manual audit (`rawOutput` empty, summary "Approved by manual review"),
  audited `2026-11-13T22:46:08Z`, closed by ship `2026-11-15T14:17:46Z`;
  `check-freshness` reports **stale (legacy audit, time gate)**.
- **Discovered-from observation (out of scope here):** release close comments
  read `Shipped in vv0.1.28` (double `v`). Track separately if it is not
  already known.

## Desired change

Run the RCA above, then apply the smallest change that makes the outcome match
the producer's expectation: a ship run must not mark content-unchanged audits
as out of date. Prefer fixing the **release write / freshness-signal** path
(e.g. preserving or re-deriving a truthful content fingerprint for the final
description on close, so content-freshness resolves) over changing the audit
verdict or fanning out re-audits. If the RCA proves the behaviour is an
intended, unavoidable consequence of the time gate, record the explanation and
the rationale in the work item and docs instead, and file a linked item for any
display-only consumer that should change.

## Key Files

- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` — release close path (`wl close`,
  `wl update --status completed --stage done`, `wl comment add`); likely site
  for avoiding an unnecessary freshness-signal bump.
- `skill/ship/scripts/audit-freshness.js` — `isAuditStale()` time gate.
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` — `getAuditStatus()`,
  `hasContentFingerprint()`, `queryContentFreshness()`,
  `attemptAuditRemediation()`.
- `skill/ship/scripts/refresh-audits.js` — `planAuditRefresh()` (time-gate
  classification; whether to consult content freshness at plan time).
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_check_audit_freshness()`,
  `_compute_content_fingerprint()`, `_extract_content_fingerprint()`,
  `AUDIT_CONTENT_FINGERPRINT_PREFIX`, `AUDIT_PERSIST_WRITE_TOLERANCE_SECONDS`,
  persistence path (`persist_audit`).
- `skill/ship/tests/` and `skill/audit/tests/` — freshness/gate test coverage.
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`, `skill/audit/SKILL.md`,
  `skill/ship/docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` — freshness-gate docs.

## Related work

- **SA-0MSRVI17W004U9G0** — Simplify audit freshness: invalidate only on this
  work item's own data change (completed, shipped v0.1.24). Introduced the
  item-data-only v2 fingerprint and the legacy time-gate fallback this item
  observes.
- **SA-0MUOO5TRU005ALBL** — Ship skill: eliminate stale-audit false blocks and
  bound release-time audit cost (completed). Added the content-fresh fast path
  so content-unchanged audits are not re-audited by the release gates.
- **SA-0MUOO5W8J001DYTI** — Ship: consume persisted audit content fingerprint
  (completed). Added `queryContentFreshness()` / `check-freshness` probe.
- **SA-0MVTU2643004QTQN** — Content-freshness contract: content-fresh audits
  are trusted regardless of `updatedAt` (completed).
- **SA-0MVAWFJXM0096FAB**, **SA-0MVAWFYKT002CQ3L** — child freshness
  fingerprint test coverage / stabilisation (completed).
- **SA-0MPE03RD0005NE0H** — ralph: skip redundant start-of-iteration audit
  when the persisted audit is up to date (completed) — adjacent freshness
  consumer.
- **WL-0MSRBFFLN005W3VT** (ContextHub worklog) — RCA: downtime dispatcher
  re-dispatches the same item; the herdr `isAuditFresh` time-based trigger is a
  separate repository concern, out of scope unless the RCA proves otherwise.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — "invalidated (out of date)" means the freshness signal, not a
  destroyed audit record.** Stored audits remain retrievable; the item is marked
  stale by the time gate / a consumer. If the producer means audits are being
  *deleted* or overwritten, re-scope.
- **Assumption — the release close path is the dominant trigger.** The observed
  evidence points at `wl close`/`wl update --status completed` bumping
  `updatedAt` after the audit; `wl sync` re-sort is a secondary candidate to
  confirm during the RCA.
- **Risk — fabricated audit metadata.** Writing a content fingerprint at close
  must not imply a new audit verdict. Preserve the original `auditedAt` and
  verdict; only record the content hash if that is truthful.
- **Risk — scope creep into herdr.** The dispatcher is a different repository;
  link rather than edit.
- **Risk — mass re-audit / cost blow-up.** Any "fix" that re-audits the backlog
  is unacceptable; the content-fresh fast path must remain.
- **Risk — regressing the block-prevention fix.** SA-0MUOO5TRU005ALBL's stale-
  audit false-block remedy must keep working.

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- **OPEN QUESTION (scope):** Does "audits invalidated (out of date)" refer to
  (a) the audit-freshness *signal* shown by consumers (herdr icon, `wl`
  display) treating a content-unchanged audit as stale, or (b) an actual loss/
  overwrite of stored audit records? — **Assumption (Map, intake):** (a). The
  store inspection shows audits present and retrievable, with staleness driven
  by `updatedAt` moving after `auditedAt`. Source: `.worklog/worklog.db`
  `audit_results` scan (1 685 audited items; 1 274 time-stale; 1 155 without a
  v2 line).
- **OPEN QUESTION (layer):** If the cause is the time gate, which layer should
  change — the release write path (avoid the unnecessary `updatedAt` bump /
  preserve the freshness signal), the freshness rule, or the display consumer
  (herdr, separate repo)? — **Assumption (Map, intake):** prefer the release
  write path or a truthful content-fingerprint preservation; keep herdr out of
  scope with a linked item. Source: RCA hypothesis, not yet producer-confirmed.
- **OPEN QUESTION (fix vs explain):** The brief is structured as
  "RCA, then fix if avoidable, else explain". If the producer already knows
  this is intended, the fix ACs can be dropped. — **Assumption (Map, intake):**
  run the RCA first; do not assume intent. Source: item seed wording ("Is this
  an intended side-effect … or … avoided").

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MPE03RD0005NE0H** – ralph: skip redundant start-of-iteration audit when persisted audit is up-to-date (completed)
- **SA-0MW0LP0OZ009OTR9** – Docs: document slot discovery, effective ceiling and slot_busy (completed)
- **SA-0MLYEOJ2N0UC3XCY** – Refactor tests for descriptor-driven audit API (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: audits, date, effect, explain, fix (+12 more)
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — matched: audits, date, effect, explain, fix (+11 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: audits, date, effect, explain, fix, former (+10 more)


---

## Plan: changelog

- **2026-11-16** — `/skill:plan SA-0MVX4EHUP0042V9G` (downtime-dispatched, herdr-downtime).
  - Pre-check: effort Small / risk Medium → full planning (above the skip threshold); plan-approval gate: not required.
  - Decomposed into 5 children (test-first dependency order):
    - SA-0MWJ4TIJT004NFJN — RCA: ship writes that invalidate audits (feature)
    - SA-0MWJ4TL8N006LYF9 — Freshness regression tests (task) — depends on F1
    - SA-0MWJ4TOMX003BZ6K — Stop ship invalidating unchanged audits (feature) — depends on F2 + F1
    - SA-0MWJ4TPHS008NOTN — Freshness documentation update (docs) — depends on F3
    - SA-0MWJ4TQMH0047HH9 — Full project suite passes (task) — depends on F3 + F4
  - Six automated review stages run on the plan (see session report): no intent-altering changes required; four redundant auto-close placeholder children were deleted after the planned children were strengthened to cover parent ACs 1/5/6/7 directly (AC coverage review: proceed, 100%).
  - Effort/risk refreshed from child aggregation: Small / Medium (score 6).
  - Open questions carried from intake remain OPEN QUESTIONs for the RCA to resolve (scope/layer/fix-vs-explain assumptions recorded by Map in the intake appendix).

# Speed up implement finish under concurrent sessions (target concurrency 6)

## Problem statement

Implement sessions that run concurrently spend the overwhelming majority of their
wall-clock waiting on a single per-repository `flock`, because `implement.py finish`
holds that lock across its **whole** commit → fast-forward → push → post-push window
and the dev-push **pre-push hook runs the full test suite (~5.4 min)** inside it.
Every concurrent `finish` therefore serialises its expensive test run behind the
others. At the intended fan-out of **up to 6 concurrent sessions**, the sixth finish
queues behind five ~5-min full-suite runs.

## Evidence (2026-11-13, AI_Hell implement-skill sessions)

Analysed the 36 worktree sessions that started with the implement skill
(`~/.pi/agent/sessions/--home-rgardler-projects-AI_Hell-.worklog-*`):

- **668 min** summed session time over a **388 min (6.5 h)** wall-clock span —
  only **1.7x effective parallelism** at a **peak measured concurrency of 4**.
- **88–93%** of each long session's wall-clock was inside `bash` tool calls
  (waiting on processes), not model reasoning or edits.
- Time buckets: **wait_for_job 249 min (37%)** (215.9 min of it lock-waits),
  own `finish` 133 min (20%), scoped tests 57 min (9%), hand-rolled
  `sleep`/`grep` polling loops 48 min (7%).
- **57** "another run holds the repository lock" refusals; **46** observed
  lock-waits averaging **4.3 min** (median 5 min, **max 21.5 min**). Worst single
  tool call: **45 min** = a `for attempt in 1..8` retry loop absorbing five
  consecutive lock holders.
- **21** non-fast-forward rebase events, each creating a new tree that re-triggers
  the full-suite pre-push gate (9 full-suite gate runs today).
- 9 sessions were **no-ops** (3 messages, ~50 s) — drive retries that immediately
  gave up.

## Users

- **Operator** running a fan-out batch of up to 6 concurrent implement sessions
  (the intended operating point) on a single repository.
- **Implement-skill sessions** (leaf and driven child) whose `finish` currently queues
  behind other sessions' full-suite runs.
- **Producers/reviewers** who need the speed-up evidenced, not asserted.

User stories:

- As an operator running up to 6 concurrent implement sessions, I want `finish` to
  complete in minutes of real work rather than tens of minutes of serialised queueing
  behind other sessions' full-suite runs, so a fan-out batch finishes in roughly the
  time of one work item rather than the sum of all of them.
- As a driven child session, I want my single `finish` call to wait boundedly on the
  lock instead of scripting retry loops.
- As a producer, I want a recorded before/after measurement before the epic is closed.

## Goal

As an operator running up to 6 concurrent implement sessions, I want `finish` to
complete in minutes of real work rather than tens of minutes of serialised
queueing behind other sessions' full-suite runs, so a fan-out batch finishes in
roughly the time of one work item rather than the sum of all of them.

## Decomposition

The epic is decomposed into five child items; together they own every acceptance
criterion below.

1. Move the dev-push full-suite gate outside the main-checkout finish lock
   (SA-0MWFJS3820032YB4) — the single biggest time sink: stop holding the exclusive
   repository lock across the ~5.4 min full-suite gate.
2. Finish wait ergonomics: one bounded internal wait, no bespoke retry loops
   (SA-0MWFJS65O005JMJF) — replace fail-fast refusals plus agent-scripted retry loops
   with one bounded internal wait that reports the holder.
3. Stop rebase-induced full-suite re-runs on dev pushes (SA-0MWFJS9OL001ZTTC) — a lost
   push race currently pays the full suite again because the rebase produces a new tree.
4. Eliminate no-op drive retries that spawn and immediately give up
   (SA-0MWFJSCPT005BO2R) — 9 of 36 sessions did no work.
5. Measure the 6-way concurrent finish fan-out and record before/after analysis
   (SA-0MWFK10NH006QI7E) — verifies the outcome ACs against real session logs; blocked
   by items 1–4.

## Acceptance criteria

- Under a 6-way concurrent `finish` fan-out, no session spends the majority of its
  wall-clock blocked on the per-repository lock (measured: median lock-wait per session < 60 s; no single lock-wait > 5 min).
- The full test suite is never executed while a single global repository lock is held (proved by inspection + test).
- A waiting `finish` performs **one** bounded internal wait rather than N fail-fast round-trips, and the skill guidance contains no bespoke `for attempt ...; wait_for_job` finish retry loops.
- A concrete before/after measurement is recorded (same 36-session style analysis).
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Safety invariants stay intact: single-owner mutation of the shared `dev` ref, the
  bounded `IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT`, and tree/provenance binding of gate verdicts
  (no verdict about a different tree/diff may be trusted).
- The dev-push gate keeps `scope=full` for release-critical refs — the speed-up must not
  weaken the release gate.
- Target concurrency is **up to 6**; designs are evaluated at that fan-out.

## Existing state

- `implement.py finish` acquires `<main-checkout>/.worklog/locks/main-checkout.lock`
  (`shared.repo_lock.RepoLock`) at Step 3c and holds it through push and post-push
  verification; `IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT` defaults to 0 (fail fast).
- `.githooks/pre-push` runs `run_tests.py --scope full --gate-commit <sha>` for
  pushes to `dev`/`main`, with a tree-keyed verdict cache (`fingerprint_kind="tree"`)
  and gate provenance lines, all of which execute inside the held finish lock today.
- Pushes to the shared `dev` ref lose the non-fast-forward race under concurrency; the
  rebase-and-retry path in `implement.py` produces a new tree and therefore a cache miss.
- `phase_drive` spawns one session per child; some spawns observe state that makes the
  child immediately terminal/blocked and exit as no-ops.

## Desired change

Concurrent `finish` runs overlap their expensive work instead of serialising on one
repository-wide critical section, and the epic's outcome is evidenced by a recorded
before/after session analysis.

## Impact

An operator can run a 6-way concurrent implement fan-out and have the batch finish in
roughly the time of one work item, instead of waiting for six serialised five-minute
test runs — while still shipping only fully tested commits.

**Key Files:**

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `phase_finish` Step 3c lock window, push/rebase retry path, `phase_drive` spawn decisions
- `skill/shared/repo_lock.py` — `RepoLock` / bounded wait for `main-checkout.lock`
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — full-suite gate, `test` semaphore lane, tree-keyed verdict cache
- `.githooks/pre-push` — dev/main full-suite gate and cache mirroring
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` and `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — finish/wait guidance to update
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_main_checkout_lock.py`, `skill/implement/tests/test_lock_timeout_isolation.py`, `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` — existing regression coverage to extend

## Related work

- Crash-safe per-repository finish lock (SA-0MVPZG3IQ009IJMO) — the lock/wait helper this epic shrinks the critical section of.
- implement.py finish: concurrent sessions orphan each other's commits via the shared local-dev fast-forward (SA-0MVNQURZM001TKJY) — established the single-owner lock invariant.
- Hermetic regression tests for finish concurrency orphans (SA-0MVPZG01J0067PC2) — concurrency test patterns to reuse.
- Defer full suite to dev-push (SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81) — why the full suite sits at the gate.
- Tree-keyed gate verdict (SA-0MVXUCGPK003G2KV) — the cache that makes verdict reuse possible.
- Session-time analysis skill (SA-0MVIKL8U7003UACM) — this epic's measurement items should reuse/feed it.
- Post-fix slot-wait re-measurement (SA-0MW7C69KU008ZT5K) — precedent methodology for before/after measurement.
- Git transport is fragile under concurrent agent runs (SA-0MW22SEMV00230O5) — push-race prior art.

## Out of scope

- Trimming the full suite's own runtime / sharding / per-file caching, and raising
  `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` — those are per-project (AI_Hell) concerns, not framework.
- Changing changed-scope test selection.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk:** moving the suite out of the lock could let an untested tree reach `dev`;
  mitigation is the tree/provenance-bound verdict and the ancestry assertion, both
  preserved by the owning children.
- **Risk:** verdict reuse after a rebase could accept a genuinely different diff;
  mitigated by provable content equality plus a negative test.
- **Risk (scope creep):** building a general lock/push queue service is out of scope;
  the children take the smallest change that meets their ACs.
- **Assumption:** the measured symptom is lock serialisation, not per-project suite
  runtime — the baseline bucket analysis supports this (37% in `wait_for_job`, 215.9 min
  of it lock-waits).
- **Assumption:** sessions of comparable work-item size are available for the "after"
  measurement; otherwise a synthetic 6-way fan-out supplies it.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What concurrency target must the design satisfy?" — Answer (operator, 2026-11-13):
  "Up to 6 concurrent implement sessions." Source: analysis comment on this item
  (SA-C0MWFJT68N001G1DR).
- Q: "Is trimming the per-project full test suite runtime in scope?" — Answer (operator,
  2026-11-13): "No — per-project (AI_Hell) suite trimming, sharding and
  `TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY` changes are out of scope for this epic." Source: same comment.
- Q: "What is the evidence base for the problem statement?" — Answer: the 2026-11-13
  AI_Hell analysis of 36 implement-skill sessions (668 min summed over a 388 min span;
  1.7x effective parallelism; 46 lock-waits, median 5 min, max 21.5 min; 21 rebases;
  9 no-op sessions). Source: comment SA-C0MWFJT68N001G1DR and the "Evidence" section
  above.
- Q: "Does the epic already own a measurement/verification item?" — Answer (this intake,
  research: `wl list --parent SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1`): no — the four original children all
  change code, so the outcome ACs had no owner; child 5
  (SA-0MWFK10NH006QI7E) was created to own them.

### Plan session (2026-11-13)

- Q: "Are further clarifying questions needed before the decomposition is final?"
  Answer (agent, research: full re-read of all five children plus repository verification
  of `implement.py` Step 3c / `DEFAULT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT`, `.githooks/pre-push`,
  `run_tests.py` tree-keyed cache and `phase_drive`): no — the four intake answers
  (concurrency target 6; per-project suite trimming out of scope; evidence base;
  measurement ownership) already fix scope, and every child's factual claims check out
  against the current code.
- Q: "Does each root cause need a separate test-only work item before implementation?"
  Answer (agent, applying the plan skill's vertical-slice rule): no — every child carries
  its own test acceptance criteria and names its test home in `**Key Files:**`, so each is
  a vertical slice (code + tests + docs) rather than a horizontal layer.
- Q: "Do the two lock-window children need sequencing?"

# Finish wait ergonomics: one bounded internal wait, no bespoke retry loops

Parent: Speed up implement finish under concurrent sessions (target concurrency 6) (SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1).

## Problem statement

`IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT` defaults to 0 (fail fast). When the lock is held, the
agent must re-enter the queue itself, so the skill guidance teaches a hand-rolled
`for attempt in 1..8; implement.py finish ... ; wait_for_job.py --pid <holder> ...`
loop. In the 2026-11-13 AI_Hell analysis this pattern produced the single worst tool
call — **45 minutes** absorbing five consecutive lock holders — and accounted for a
large share of the 37% `wait_for_job` time plus 48 min (7%) of separate `sleep`/`grep`
polling loops. Each fail-fast refusal is also a wasted model round-trip.

## Users

- **Operator** running a fan-out batch: wants predictable, minimal waiting per session.
- **Implement-skill session** that currently has to script retry loops around
  `implement.py finish`.

User stories:

- As an implement-skill session, I want one `finish` call to wait internally on the
  lock (bounded, with progress) so I do not burn model round-trips on retry loops.
- As an operator watching a batch, I want a waiting session to report who holds the
  lock and to fail with an actionable message only when the bound expires.

## Goal

As an operator, I want a waiting `finish` to perform **one** bounded internal wait on
the flock (with progress), instead of the agent scripting fail-fast retry loops around
it, so concurrent finishes do not multiply round-trips and confusing logs.

## Approach

- Make a positive bounded `IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT` the guidance default (or
  document setting it) so `finish` waits internally on the flock up to a generous
  bound, emitting progress.
- Remove the `for attempt in ... ; implement.py finish ... ; wait_for_job` retry-loop
  guidance from the implement skill; replace with the single bounded-wait instruction.
- Ensure the internal wait reports the holder and honours `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM` cleanly.

## Acceptance criteria

- `implement.py finish` with a positive `IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT` waits on the
  lock internally within the bound, reporting the holder, and fails with an
  actionable message only when the bound expires.
- The implement skill docs contain no bespoke finish retry-loop pattern; they instruct
  a single bounded wait.
- A waiting `finish` performs **one** bounded internal wait rather than N fail-fast round-trips, and the skill guidance contains no bespoke `for attempt ...; wait_for_job` finish retry loops.
- A test covers: lock held → `finish` waits → holder releases → `finish` proceeds
  (no fail-fast refusal).
- Regression test that the wait is bounded (never hangs) and is signal-safe.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The wait must stay bounded: a configured timeout always terminates the wait with an
  actionable refusal naming the holder and the lock path.
- `SIGINT`/`SIGTERM` must release the held lock and the child lock and exit cleanly
  (no orphaned locks).
- Default behaviour must stay safe for unattended sessions: a positive bound must not
  be able to wedge a batch indefinitely.
- Out of scope: changing the single-owner lock semantics or removing the lock.

## Existing state

- `DEFAULT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT = 0.0` (fail fast), env `IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT`,
  read by `_finish_lock_timeout()`; the bounded wait lives in
  `shared.repo_lock.RepoLock` via `acquire_main_checkout_lock`.
- The implement skill documents the current fail-fast behaviour, and sessions work
  around it with `for attempt ... ; wait_for_job.py --pid <holder>` loops.
- Lock holders are recorded with pid/host metadata, so the holder can already be named
  in a refusal.

## Desired change

`finish` performs one bounded internal wait with progress and holder reporting; the
skill guidance describes that single call instead of a bespoke retry loop.

## Impact

An operator's concurrent batch stops multiplying model round-trips and multi-minute
tool calls on lock contention: a waiting session reports who holds the lock and
proceeds automatically once released.

**Key Files:**

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `DEFAULT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT`, `ENV_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT`, `_finish_lock_timeout()`, `acquire_main_checkout_lock` call in `phase_finish`
- `skill/shared/repo_lock.py` — bounded wait implementation and holder reporting
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — guidance that must lose the bespoke retry-loop pattern
- `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_main_checkout_lock.py` and `skill/implement/tests/test_lock_timeout_isolation.py` — test homes for the wait behaviour
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — timeout documentation

## Related work

- Parent epic: Speed up implement finish under concurrent sessions (target concurrency 6) (SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1)
- Crash-safe per-repository finish lock (SA-0MVPZG3IQ009IJMO) — the lock/wait helper.
- implement test suite inherits IMPLEMENT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT from the ambient environment and hangs for hours (SA-0MVY0G5EH000LIMB) — timeout inheritance hazard to keep in mind.
- Sibling item: Move the dev-push full-suite gate outside the main-checkout finish lock (SA-0MWFJS3820032YB4) — the other half of lock-wait reduction.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk (scope creep):** building a general-purpose lock queue service is out of scope;
  this item is one bounded wait inside `finish`.
- **Risk:** a long default bound could make an unattended batch appear hung; mitigation:
  progress output plus a clear expiry message, and the default chosen deliberately
  (documented) rather than "infinite".
- **Assumption:** the holder pid/identity metadata recorded by `RepoLock` is sufficient
  to name the holder in progress output.
- **Assumption:** removing the retry-loop guidance from the skill does not break driven
  sessions, which call `finish` once per child.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required for this item. Evidence base: 2026-11-13 AI_Hell
36-session analysis on the parent epic (SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1, comment
SA-C0MWFJT68N001G1DR), including the 45-minute worst-case tool call and the 48 min of
`sleep`/`grep` polling. Researched in the repository: `_finish_lock_timeout()` /
`DEFAULT_FINISH_LOCK_TIMEOUT` in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` and the bounded
wait in `skill/shared/repo_lock.py`.

# Stop rebase-induced full-suite re-runs on dev pushes

Parent: Speed up implement finish under concurrent sessions (target concurrency 6) (SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1).

## Problem statement

Because concurrent finishes push to the shared `dev` ref, pushes frequently lose the
non-fast-forward race: in the 2026-11-13 AI_Hell analysis there were **21** rebase
events. Each rebase rewrites the commit onto a new base, producing a **new tree**, which
misses the tree-keyed gate cache and **re-runs the ~5.4-min full suite** inside the
lock. So a single work item can pay the full-suite cost repeatedly (e.g. AH-0MWEZZE5U,
AH-0MWEYVRUX and others showed 2–3 rebase rounds each).

## Users

- **Operator** running a concurrent fan-out batch into `dev`.
- **Implement-skill session** that loses the push race and today pays another full-suite
  run after rebasing.

User stories:

- As an implement-skill session that lost the push race, I want to rebase and push
  without re-running the full suite, because my change content did not change.
- As an operator, I want the number of full-suite gate runs in a batch to stay close to
  the number of work items, not a multiple of it.

## Goal

As an operator, I want a rebased push not to re-run the full suite when the change
content is unchanged, so a lost push race costs seconds, not another 5 minutes.

## Approach (options to weigh)

- Serialise dev pushes (a short push queue / fast-forward retry that rebases only the
  ref, reusing the already-green tree verdict where the tree is provably identical).
- Or key the gate verdict on the **commit's change set / content hash** rather than the
  full tree, so a pure rebase (same diff, different base) reuses the verdict.
- Or batch dev advancement so a batch is rebased once.

## Acceptance criteria

- A push that loses the non-fast-forward race and is rebased onto a new base does
  **not** re-execute the full suite when the tree/diff is provably unchanged (cache
  hit demonstrated in a test).
- The safety property is preserved: a verdict is never reused for a tree/diff that
  actually differs.
- The number of full-suite gate runs for a concurrent fan-out drops measurably
  (recorded before/after).
- An automated test covers the rebase-then-push path reusing a prior green verdict, and
  a negative test proves a genuinely different tree/diff still misses the cache.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- The gate must remain evidence about the **pushed** commit: a verdict may only be
  reused when the tested content is provably identical to what is pushed.
- No weakening of the release gate for `dev`/`main`; `scope=full` stays mandatory.
- Cannot rely on changing per-project suite runtime or sharding.
- Out of scope: redesigning the git transport retry policy for auth/transport failures.

## Existing state

- `.githooks/pre-push` runs `run_tests.py --scope full --gate-commit <sha>` for
  `dev`/`main` pushes and mirrors gate cache entries into the main checkout's
  `.worklog/cache`.
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` keys cached verdicts with `fingerprint_kind="tree"`
  and records `gate-subject` / `gate-verdict` provenance (`tree=`, cache hit/miss + age).
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` raises a recoverable non-fast-forward error
  carrying a `rebase_cmd` hint, so the caller rebases onto `origin/dev` and retries —
  producing a new tree and therefore a cache miss today.

## Desired change

A rebased push of provably unchanged content reuses the existing green verdict, so a
lost push race no longer costs another full-suite run.

## Impact

Losing a push race in a concurrent batch costs seconds instead of another five-minute
full-suite run, so a batch's total gate time stops multiplying with the number of
rebases.

**Key Files:**

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — tree-keyed verdict cache, `--gate-commit` binding, `gate-verdict` provenance
- `.githooks/pre-push` — gate invocation and cache mirroring for dev/main pushes
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `PUSH_FAILURE_NON_FAST_FORWARD`, the non-fast-forward exception and its `rebase_cmd` retry path
- `tests/test_pre_push_gate_reuse.py` and `tests/test_test_cache.py` — gate cache/reuse tests to extend
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — push retry / gate documentation

## Related work

- Parent epic: Speed up implement finish under concurrent sessions (target concurrency 6) (SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1)
- Tree-keyed gate verdict (SA-0MVXUCGPK003G2KV) — the cache this item extends.
- Defer full suite to dev-push (SA-0MVECQUGF0064U81) — why the gate exists.
- Git transport is fragile under concurrent agent runs: transient SSH auth failures and push races make leaf finish fail after the work has landed (SA-0MW22SEMV00230O5) — push-race handling prior art.
- Sibling item: Move the dev-push full-suite gate outside the main-checkout finish lock (SA-0MWFJS3820032YB4) — both reduce gate cost under concurrency.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk (safety):** reusing a verdict for a different diff would let an untested change
  reach `dev`; mitigation: reuse only on provable content equality, with a negative test.
- **Risk (scope creep):** batching dev advancement is a larger refactor; treat it as the
  fallback option, preferring the verdict-keying change.
- **Assumption:** a pure rebase produces an identical diff (so a change-set key would
  hit) even though the tree SHA differs.
- **Assumption:** the pre-push hook can be told the intended verdict key without
  weakening the "evidence about the pushed commit" property.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required for this item. Evidence: 21 rebase events and the
2–3-round repeats (AH-0MWEZZE5U, AH-0MWEYVRUX) in the 2026-11-13 AI_Hell analysis on the
parent epic (SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1, comment SA-C0MWFJT68N001G1DR). Researched in the
repository: `.githooks/pre-push` gate invocation and cache mirroring,
`run_tests.py` tree-keyed cache, and the non-fast-forward rebase-and-retry path in
`implement.py`.

Deterministic clobber injection for the audit lifecycle restore paths: an

## Objective

Add the read-only, unit-testable **bump preflight helper** used by the ship skill's new version-bump evaluation step. It gathers the release candidates and renders a compact review packet. It performs **no judgement and no mutation** — the agent judges, the producer approves.

## User Story

As the PI agent running `/skill:ship release`, I want a single helper that gathers every release candidate and renders the evidence I need to judge the release's importance, so that my patch/minor/major call is based on the items' content rather than guesswork.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The ship skill's release workflow gains a startup **version-bump evaluation** step that runs before any git mutation and gathers every release candidate (`wl list --stage in_review`) with enough context for a judgement: ID, title, type, priority, `## Impact`/user story and a short description excerpt.
- New module `skill/ship/scripts/release/bump-preflight.js` exports a `gatherReleaseCandidates` (name may vary) that resolves candidates through an **injectable fetch boundary** (default `getCandidateItems()` from `check-audit-gate.js`); tests inject fakes and never read the live worklog.
- The helper enriches each candidate with the fields needed to judge importance: `id`, `title`, `issueType`, `priority`, the `## Impact` section or user story, and a truncated description excerpt. It tolerates missing fields (falls back to the title/id and an empty excerpt) without throwing.
- The helper renders a review packet (Markdown or plain text) that includes: the current version, the three candidate outcomes computed via the **existing** `bump-version.js` arithmetic (`bumpVersion`), and the per-item evidence listed above. It reuses `resolveVersionSource`/`bumpVersion` (no duplicated semver arithmetic).
- Minor bumps reset `z` to `0`, and major bumps reset `y` and `z` to `0`, reusing the existing `release/bump-version.js` semantics (`bumpVersion`) rather than duplicating version arithmetic anywhere in the new helper.
- An **empty or unreadable candidate set** fails safe: the helper reports `patch` as the proposal, logs a warning explaining why, and never throws or blocks a release.
- Gathering/rendering is **purely read-only** — the helper performs no `git`, tag, PR, or `wl` mutation.
- `skill/ship/tests/test_bump_preflight.mjs` covers: candidate gathering via the injected boundary, rendering of every packet field, the empty candidate set (patch + warning), and that `minor`/`major` outcomes reset the lower components correctly (delegated to `bumpVersion`).
- Tests pass via the test skill (`run_tests.py --scope changed`, node suite) and touch no live worklog or real git state.

## Minimal Implementation

1. Write the failing test file first (`test_bump_preflight.mjs`, `node:test`).
2. Add `skill/ship/scripts/release/bump-preflight.js` with an exported preflight function accepting `{ getCandidateItemsFn, repoRoot }` injection.
3. Project `version` from the resolved version source; compute `patch`/`minor`/`major` outcomes with `bumpVersion`.
4. Render the packet with a stable, agent-readable layout; truncate description excerpts (e.g. ~200 chars).
5. Return a structured result (`{ candidates, currentVersion, proposals, proposedBump, warning }`) as well as the rendered text, so tests can assert fields directly.
6. Export a small render/format function so the workflow contract test can rely on a stable API.

## Key Files

- `skill/ship/scripts/release/bump-preflight.js` (new)
- `skill/ship/tests/test_bump_preflight.mjs` (new)
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` (reuse `getCandidateItems`)
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/bump-version.js` (reuse `resolveVersionSource`, `bumpVersion`)

## Constraints

- No issue-type or priority classifier — the helper only gathers/renders evidence.
- No mutation and no new git side effects.
- Empty/unreadable candidates default to `patch` with a warning.

## Deliverables

- `bump-preflight.js` with tests, passing the changed-scope suite.

## Goal

Remove entries from the tracked Pi configuration (`.pi-config/agent/models.json` and any matching `settings.json` patterns) that name models the provider does not actually serve, and canonicalise the ids that only work as undocumented aliases — so agents stop selecting an entry that fails with a 400 at request time.

User story: As a producer, I want the tracked Pi configuration to list only models that the configured providers actually serve, so that a session never fails mid-task because it selected a phantom model entry.

## Evidence (probed 2026-02-08 against live provider endpoints)

Local Proxy — `GET http://192.168.0.199:8000/v1/models` returns `embed, private, plan, author, code, compact`. Chat probes:
- `plan` -> HTTP 200; `compact` -> HTTP 200
- `qwen3` -> HTTP 400 `model 'qwen3' not found`
- `gpt120` -> HTTP 400 `model 'gpt120' not found`

deepseek — `GET https://api.deepseek.com/models` returns `deepseek-flash`, `deepseek-v4-pro`:
- `deepseek-v4-pro` -> in catalogue, valid
- `deepseek-v4-flash` -> NOT in catalogue; accepted only as an undocumented alias (HTTP 200 reporting `"model":"deepseek-flash"`). Canonical id `deepseek-flash` also carries correct metadata: contextWindow 1048576, maxTokens 393216, text+image input, effort levels low/high/max

MunitoAI — `GET https://api.munito.ai/inference/v1/models` lists both tracked ids; both valid (no change)

opencode / opencode-go `modelOverrides` — live `GET /models` returns `api_key_expired` (separate credential defect, out of scope). Against the cached catalogue (`~/.pi/agent/models-store.json`):
- `opencode`: `qwen3.5-plus`, `qwen3.6-plus` present -> valid
- `opencode-go`: `qwen3.7-plus`, `qwen3.8-max` present -> valid; `qwen3.6-plus` and `qwen3.7-max` absent -> suspect

## Scope

In scope: `.pi-config/agent/models.json` (tracked), plus `settings.json` `enabledModels` patterns if they reference a removed entry.
Out of scope: expired `opencode` / `opencode-go` API keys (file separately); adding models that are served but not tracked (`compact`, `private`, `embed`) unless the producer asks.

**Key Files:**
- `.pi-config/agent/models.json` — tracked model configuration
- `.pi-config/agent/settings.json` — tracked settings with `enabledModels`
- `scripts/merge_pi_agent_config.py` — merge helper (non-destructive by design)
- `scripts/install_pi.sh` — installation script; invokes the merge helper
- `tests/test_merge_pi_agent_config.py` — merge helper tests
- `tests/test_models_config_qwen_thinking.py` — Qwen thinking override tests; asserts tracked overrides exist, so must be updated when ids are removed
- `.pi-config/agent/retired-models.json` — **new** tracked source of truth for pruned ids (see Producer decisions)

## Acceptance criteria

1. `Local Proxy` provider lists no model id that the proxy rejects: `qwen3` and `gpt120` are removed.
2. `deepseek` provider references only catalogued ids: `deepseek-v4-flash` is replaced by `deepseek-flash`, with metadata matching the catalogue (contextWindow, maxTokens, input modalities, effort map).
3. `deepseek-v4-pro` is retained and its **full** metadata reconciled with the catalogue, not only the two known deltas: `contextWindow` 1000000 -> 1048576, `maxTokens` 384000 -> 393216, `input` modalities matching the catalogue, and `thinkingLevelMap` / `reasoningEffortMap` reconciled so a level is not `null` in `thinkingLevelMap` while simultaneously mapped to `"high"` in `reasoningEffortMap`. The catalogue metadata captured by the AC 6 probe is the authority.
4. `opencode-go` `modelOverrides` entries not present in the cached catalogue (`~/.pi/agent/models-store.json`; the live `GET /models` returns `api_key_expired`) are removed: `qwen3.6-plus`, `qwen3.7-max`; entries confirmed present are retained unchanged.
5. `settings.json` `enabledModels` contains no pattern that matches nothing after the change (`pi models` emits no "No models match pattern" warning).
6. Verification is a **one-off command, not a committed script**: (i) each provider's `GET {baseUrl}/models` response diffed against the tracked ids, (ii) the deepseek catalogue metadata for `deepseek-flash` and `deepseek-v4-pro` (used to settle AC 2 and AC 3), and (iii) `pi models` showing no "No models match pattern" warning. The exact commands and their captured output are recorded in a comment on this item. No `scripts/` checker is added by this item.
7. **Prune semantics in the merge helper (producer option B).** `scripts/merge_pi_agent_config.py` gains explicit prune support driven by a tracked retired-ids source, and prunes those ids (model entries *and* their `modelOverrides` keys) from the destination while still preserving every **unlisted** local-only provider, model, override and top-level key. After `scripts/install_pi.sh`, `~/.pi/agent/models.json` contains none of `qwen3`, `gpt120`, `deepseek-v4-flash`, `qwen3.6-plus`, `qwen3.7-max`; the prune is reported in the merge summary and a backup is written before the modification.
8. Tests cover the merge/validation behaviour where the repository already has test coverage for `scripts/merge_pi_agent_config.py`.
8a. `tests/test_models_config_qwen_thinking.py` is updated: the `OPENCODE_GO_QWEN` set is reduced to the retained ids (`qwen3.7-plus`, `qwen3.8-max`), and its assertions no longer require `qwen3.6-plus` / `qwen3.7-max` on `opencode-go`.
8b. `tests/test_merge_pi_agent_config.py` covers the new prune behaviour: a retired id present in the destination is removed (both as a model entry and as a `modelOverrides` key); an **unlisted** local-only model/override is preserved verbatim; a retired id absent from the destination is a no-op; a second run is an idempotent no-op (no second backup, no duplicated entries); and the merge summary reports the prunes.

## Producer decisions (recorded 2026-11-17)

1. **Stale-id purge → option B**: extend `merge_pi_agent_config.py` with prune semantics rather than relying on a manual machine cleanup or relaxing AC 7. Proposed mechanism (implementation detail, may be adjusted by the implementer as long as the AC 7/AC 8b behaviour holds): a new tracked file `.pi-config/agent/retired-models.json` maps provider -> retired ids; the merge helper reads it when present, prunes those models and `modelOverrides` keys from the destination, reports each removal in its summary, and keeps preserving everything unlisted.
2. **`deepseek-v4-pro` metadata → reconcile fully** (AC 3): `input` modalities and the thinking/effort maps are reconciled too, not just `contextWindow`/`maxTokens`.
3. **Verification → one-off**: a recorded command and its captured output on this item; no committed `scripts/` checker and no `docs/dev/skills-script-paths.md` entry.

## Assumptions

- The proxy `/models` endpoint is authoritative for Local Proxy model ids (probe-confirmed by 400 responses).
- `deepseek-v4-flash` -> `deepseek-flash` is a rename, not a second model, because the server reports `deepseek-flash` in the response body.
- opencode-go catalogue validity could not be probed live; the cached store is treated as the best available evidence and will be re-checked if a key is restored.

Agents can no longer select a Pi model entry that fails with a 400, so sessions stop dying mid-task on phantom models.

## Goal

Pin the spawn-failure classifier's vocabulary and fail-safe **before** any retry code exists, so the drive loop can only ever retry a genuine provider/model-resolution failure.

User story: As an implement-skill maintainer, I want the spawn-failure classification to be table-driven and tested first, so extending the infrastructure-retry budget to spawn-time failures can never silently retry a real defect.

## Context

`CUR-0MWL0EBP30071E1J` (games_curator) reports driven child sessions dying at startup with `No models match pattern "MunitoAI/*"` and aborting the drive chain. Upstream plan: features F1–F3 + F5 live in this repository; the config half is folded into `SA-0MWL5AL4B004X0FN`. This item is **F1 — test-first**.

Findings from the planning session (code-grounded):

- `_default_session_spawner` reports a non-zero exit as `Child session for <id> exited with code N: <5-line tail>` — the provider text arrives **inside `reason`**.
- `_pane_session_spawner` reports `Failed to start the pane agent for <id>: …` or `Pane agent for <id> did not complete: …`.
- `classify_finish_failure` + `FINISH_INFRA_REFUSALS` is the existing table-driven infra vocabulary, but it is **finish-only**; there is no spawn-side classifier.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A new `classify_spawn_failure(reason)` helper exists in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` returning `{kind, reason, provider, remedy}` and is driven by an explicit allow-list table (mirroring `FINISH_INFRA_REFUSALS`), never by prose sniffing in `phase_drive`.
- Tests (written first, failing before the helper exists) assert: a headless `Child session for X exited with code 1: … No models match pattern "MunitoAI/*"` reason classifies as `kind == "infrastructure"` with `provider == "MunitoAI"` and a non-empty remedy.
- The pane flavours (`Failed to start the pane agent for X: …` and `Pane agent for X did not complete: …`) carrying the same provider text classify as `infrastructure`.
- Fail-safe is pinned: an unclassified reason (a Python traceback tail, an arbitrary message, an empty string, `None`) classifies as `kind == "unknown"` — never `infrastructure`.
- A `timed out` reason is not reclassified as provider-infrastructure (the timeout path keeps its own reconciliation semantics).
- The remedy text names the concrete action (drop the unservable pattern from `enabledModels`, or provide the missing API key) and is asserted by at least one test.
- Tests live in `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py` (the existing home for drive classification tests).

## Implementation sketch

1. Add the failing tests in `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py`.
2. Add `SPAWN_INFRA_REASONS` (allow-list of provider/model-resolution fragments) and `classify_spawn_failure(reason)` beside `classify_finish_failure`.
3. Reuse the existing `_describe_*`-style description idiom so F2 can surface `step`/`reason` in `children_driven`.

## Notes

- Test-first ordering is mandatory: this item lands before F2 so the vocabulary is fixed by tests.
- Do not widen `PANE_CHILD_ENV_KEYS`; no secret may reach `pane split --env`.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
- `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py`

## Impact

A maintainer can extend the drive loop's infrastructure retries to spawn-time provider failures knowing the classifier can only ever match a real model-resolution error, so a genuine defect still hard-stops the chain.

## Goal

A provider/model-resolution failure at child spawn is retried **inside the same `drive` invocation** on the existing bounded infra-retry budget instead of stopping the chain with `failed_child`.

User story: As an operator running `implement.py drive <epic>`, I want a transient model-routing failure in a child session to be retried automatically, so a healthy child is not abandoned and the chain does not stop.

## Context

`CUR-0MWL0EBP30071E1J` (games_curator) reports five child-session aborts across one drive run (children `CUR-0MWKPMVRH00780TO` ×2, `CUR-0MWKPMWGL005EKZF`, `CUR-0MWKPMX3M0052ZOL` ×2); each child completed on the next `drive` invocation with no code change. This item is **F2** of the upstream plan and depends on **F1** (`classify_spawn_failure` + its tests).

Current behaviour: `phase_drive`'s non-success branch runs `_reconcile_spawn_failure` → `record_spawn_failure` → `_release_orphaned_child_claim` → `report["failed_child"]` + `break`. The existing infra-retry path (`--infra-retry-limit`, `DEFAULT_INFRA_RETRY_LIMIT = 5`, `_drive_infra_backoff_delay`) covers **only** `finish` refusals and deliberately never spawns a session.

## Acceptance Criteria

- After `_reconcile_spawn_failure` reports **non-terminal**, a spawn failure classified `infrastructure` by `classify_spawn_failure` consumes one slot of `--infra-retry-limit` (default 5), sleeps `_drive_infra_backoff_delay(attempt)` and re-spawns the same child within the same invocation — no manual re-run.
- The `children_driven` entry for the retry is `result: "infra-retry"` and carries `step`, `reason`, `attempt` and a `message` naming the provider and model, reusing the additive reporting shape of the finish infra-retry.
- Budget exhaustion produces a chain-stop message naming the provider/model **and an actionable remedy**, instead of a bare `No models match pattern …`; the remedy directive is asserted in a test.
- Ordering is correct and pinned by a test: a child reconciled `completed-late` (already terminal) is **never** retried and no second session is spawned.
- Fail-safe preserved and pinned by a test: an unclassified spawn failure still hard-stops with `report["failed_child"]` and is never retried.
- Retrying does not duplicate side effects: the per-child lock is not re-acquired while held, no second worktree is created, and `record_spawn_failure` evidence is not re-written for an attempt that never produced work.
- The shared budget is documented: `infra_retries[child_id]` is one counter across finish-refusals and spawn retries, and the counter plus `infra_retry_limit` remain present in the drive report.
- Tests use a fake spawner that fails with the provider reason twice and then succeeds on a 5-slot budget, plus the exhaustion, completed-late and unclassified cases (`tests/test_implement_drive.py`, `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py`).

## Implementation sketch

1. Extract the retry decision from the finish infra-retry block and call it on the spawn-failure path, **after** reconciliation and before `failed_child`/`break`.
2. Reuse `infra_retries` / `_drive_infra_backoff_delay`; record the `children_driven` entry with the classified provider reason.
3. Re-enter the loop for the same child (`continue`) rather than spawning a different one.

## Constraints

- `PANE_CHILD_ENV_KEYS` stays `(DRIVE_RECURSION_ENV, WORKTREE_ENV, ENV_LOCK_TOKEN)` — no new secrets in argv.
- The commit-preservation gate, `reset-for-retry`, the spawn-failure evidence record (`SA-0MWGZ8NWP009QD8G`), the per-child lock and the terminality reconciliation keep their current semantics; this extends them.
- No session may be spawned for a child that reconciliation proved terminal.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
- `tests/test_implement_drive.py`
- `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py`

## Impact

An operator running a driven epic no longer loses a multi-minute child session — or the whole chain — to an intermittent model-routing error, so a `drive` run becomes self-healing.

## Goal

A child whose session never started because the model could not be resolved ends `open` with an empty assignee and a diagnosable comment naming the provider/model and the remedy — never `in-progress` with an empty assignee.

User story: As an operator, I want a failed child to be left startable so the next sweep or `drive` reclaims it without manual cleanup, and I want an actionable remedy instead of `No models match pattern MunitoAI/*`.

## Context

This item is **F3** of the upstream plan for `CUR-0MWL0EBP30071E1J` (games_curator) and depends on **F2** (classification + bounded retry), because release happens only when the infra budget is **exhausted**.

Design tension resolved in planning: `_release_orphaned_child_claim` **deliberately clears only the assignee and keeps `in-progress`**, so `finish` / `drive --finalise-stranded` recovery still applies to a session that was killed (timeout/signal). That rationale does not hold for a provider failure: the session never started, so the child has no worktree work to finish or finalise. The two paths therefore diverge deliberately, and both must be pinned by tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

- When the infra-retry budget is exhausted for a `classify_spawn_failure`-classified `infrastructure` failure, the child is written `status: open` with an empty assignee.
- No claim is released before the retry budget is exhausted — pinned by a test asserting the child is still `in-progress` between retry attempts (no sweep can reclaim it mid-retry).
- A comment on the child names the provider and model, states that the session never started, and gives the actionable remedy (drop the unservable pattern from `enabledModels`, or supply the missing provider API key).
- The existing timeout/signal path is unchanged: `_release_orphaned_child_claim` still leaves the item `in-progress` with the assignee cleared — pinned by a regression test.
- The release write is durable (via `StatusLifecycle`, not a raw `wl update` in a subprocess) and idempotent: re-running the release path on an already-`open` child is a no-op that neither errors nor emits a duplicate comment.
- The drive report's `children_driven`/`failure` entry records the release outcome (previous status/assignee) so the operator can see it from the report alone.
- Tests cover the release path (child ends `open` with empty assignee), the pre-exhaustion guard, and the timeout-path regression.

## Implementation sketch

1. Add a narrowly-scoped release helper (e.g. `_release_provider_failed_child`) beside `_release_orphaned_child_claim`, reusing `StatusLifecycle.update_status(child, "open", assignee="")`, and call it only from the exhausted-provider branch.
2. Post the remedy comment through the existing `wl_add_comment` helper.
3. Record `release` fields in the `children_driven` entry and in `report`.

## Constraints

- Do not widen `PANE_CHILD_ENV_KEYS`.
- `needsProducerReview` is never set by this helper; the only persistent hold remains that flag (per the assignee-release invariant).
- A terminal child (reconciled `completed-late`) is never touched.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py`
- `tests/test_implement_drive_recovery.py`

## Impact

An operator no longer finds a stranded `in-progress` child (invisible to `wl next`) after a model-routing failure — the child is simply reclaimable on the next sweep, with a comment that says what to fix.

## Goal

The implement-skill reference documents the new spawn-time provider-failure recovery path — the infra retry, the `infra-retry` spawn verdict, the release-to-`open` distinction and the configuration remedy — so an operator can diagnose the failure from the docs and the drive report alone.

User story: As an operator whose drive run stopped, I want the reference to tell me what the `children_driven` entry means and what to fix, instead of decoding `No models match pattern "MunitoAI/*"`.

## Context

This item is **F5** of the upstream plan for `CUR-0MWL0EBP30071E1J` (games_curator) and depends on **F2** and **F3** (and on the config fold in `SA-0MWL5AL4B004X0FN`) so the docs describe behaviour that exists.

Existing doc homes to update: the "Drive failure recovery: bounded finish attempts, reconciliation and reset" section (including its verdict table around the `infra-retry` row and the `failed` row) and the "Spawn-failure evidence" section of `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` documents the spawn-time infrastructure retry: which failures are classified, that it reuses `--infra-retry-limit` and its backoff, and that it re-spawns the same child inside the same invocation.
- The verdict/`children_driven` table states that a spawn-time provider retry is recorded as `result: "infra-retry"` with `step`, `reason`, `attempt` and a provider-naming message, and the `failed` row states when the retry is *not* taken (unclassified reason, or a child already reconciled terminal).
- The spawn-failure-evidence section states the two release semantics and why they differ: a killed/timed-out session keeps `in-progress` (so `finish` / `--finalise-stranded` still apply), while a provider failure that never started a session is released to `open` with an empty assignee.
- The configuration remedy is documented (drop the unservable `enabledModels` pattern; the tracked `.pi-config/agent/settings.json` is the durable source because the merge unions tracked patterns into `~/.pi/agent/settings.json`), including how to reverse it.
- The docs-integrity test `tests/test_implement_docs_drive_recovery.py` is updated to cover the new documented statements (a drifting doc fails the suite).
- No code behaviour is documented that the shipped F2/F3 implementation does not provide (cross-checked against the code, not written from this description alone).

## Implementation sketch

1. Read the shipped F2/F3 code, then update the two sections and the table rows.
2. Extend `tests/test_implement_docs_drive_recovery.py` with assertions for the new wording/keys.
3. Keep wording consistent with the existing table's vocabulary (`infra-retry`, `failed`, `step`, `reason`, `attempt`).

**Key Files:**
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md`
- `tests/test_implement_docs_drive_recovery.py`

## Impact

An operator reading a stopped drive report can tell a transient provider failure from a real defect and knows the one-line config fix, without reading the drive source.
